paper_title: Not a COINcidence: Sub-Quadratic Asynchronous Byzantine Agreement WHP
statement: Our algorithm solves Byzantine Agreement with high probability. It would be interesting to understand whether some of the problem’s properties can be satisfied with probability 1, while keeping the sub-quadratic communication cost. In addition, in order to achieve the constant success rate of the coin and guarantee the committees’ properties, we bounded  from below by a constant. This bound prevented us from achieving optimal resilience. The question whether it is possible to relax this bound to allow better resilience remains open.
context: We have presented the first sub-quadratic asynchronous Byzantine Agreement algorithm. To construct the algorithm, we introduced two techniques. First, we presented a shared coin algorithm that requires a trusted PKI and uses VRFs. Second, we formalized VRF-based committee sampling in the asynchronous model for the first time. Our algorithm solves Byzantine Agreement with high probability. It would be interesting to understand whether some of the problem’s properties can be satisfied with probability 1, while keeping the sub-quadratic communication cost. In addition, in order to achieve the constant success rate of the coin and guarantee the committees’ properties, we bounded  from below by a constant. This bound prevented us from achieving optimal resilience. The question whether it is possible to relax this bound to allow better resilience remains open.
